newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally, end strong on bottom-fishing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally, end strong on bottom-fishing.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended strong as foreign and domestic buyers snapped up bargain stocks in late trade.

"We think this is a good time to acquire positions in the market, and investors seem to also," said Daniel Romo, equity analyst at the Bancomer brokerage. "They're beginning to buy on favourable expectations for quarterly reports."
The blue chip IPC index closed up 50.16 points, or 1.55 percent, at 3,286.48. Volume picked up after midsession, particularly in blue chips, and stood at 89.1 million shares for the session.
Traders noted the presence of market heavyweights like brewers Grupo Modelo and steelmakers Hylsamex on the percentage gainers' list.

Modelo and Hylsamex closed up 1.95 pesos (30 cents) and 1.35 pesos (18 cents), respectively, at 40.75 ($5.42) and 29.50 ($3.92). This came after several days in which infrequently traded stocks had come to the fore.
"The market had brought blue chips down to support levels, and that's where buyers stepped in, as with Modelo and Hylsamex," an equity analyst said.

Another notable gainer was holding company Grupo Carso whose A1 series stock closed up 1.40 pesos (19 cents) to 36.00 pesos ($4.79) on news that its telecommunications subsidiary was to increase its capital by 682.5 million pesos ($91 million).
A total of 108 stocks changed hands on the broad market, with winners outnumbering losers 49 to 35.
